desks.title: Wandoo Hill Roasters — identity refresh
desks.description: A small-batch roaster's new mark, type and colour, taken from three concept routes to a system that works on a 250 g bag, a cup sleeve and a 16 px favicon.
desks.brief:
## Wandoo Hill Roasters — identity refresh

**Client** Wandoo Hill Roasters · Dimitri (owner), Yasmin (head roaster)
**Stage** Round 2 of 3 · review @+4d · bag artwork to the printer @+8d
**Scope** mark, wordmark, colour, type and 10 applications · **Quoted** 56 hours

### The problem with the old identity
A script wordmark that disappears below 40 px, five browns nobody can tell apart on a shelf, and no rules — every café menu has drifted somewhere different.

### Direction (Route B, approved in round 1)
- A single-line hill mark that holds at 16 px
- Two neutrals doing the work, one warm accent (Ember), and Eucalypt for the single-origin range
- A sturdy display serif for headings, a humanist sans for everything else

### Round 2
Bag range, cup sleeve and wholesale price list, on the approved mark. 42 of 56 quoted hours used, with 3 applications not started. The mark ran 2 hours over and the bags still need 6, which leaves 8 hours for the menu board and social templates against 10 quoted — **packaging gets the remaining hours, menu board and social templates get templates, not bespoke layouts.**

callout.title: Ember can't carry small text
callout.body: Ember on Paper measures 3.3:1 — large headings only. On Crema it's 2.7:1 and fails even that. Ember stays in the illustration and large headings on Paper; all small type on the sleeve, bag back panels and price list moves to Bark, 9.8:1 on Crema.

chart.title: Hours logged vs quoted, by type

children.label: Too close to the old badge?
Foil on the 1 kg bag — cost?

blocks.p: Route B is the only route that survives the smallest uses — a 16 px favicon and a stamped cup lid — without a second version. One line, one weight, drawn from the ridge behind the roastery.

Two neutrals carry everything: Bark for text, Crema and Paper for grounds. Ember is the warm accent, kept to the illustration and large headings because it can't pass contrast as small text. Eucalypt marks the single-origin range; Paper type on Eucalypt measures 5.0:1.

ul: Display serif for headings, set tight, never below 24 pt
Humanist sans for text and price lists — tested at 7 pt on the sleeve proof
The old script wordmark retires; Dimitri to confirm at the review @+4d

blocks.h4: What round 2 asks the client to approve

ol: Bag range: Crema for blends, Eucalypt for single origin

notes.title: Round 1 feedback — and what I did with it
notes.body:
Dimitri: loves the hill line, wants it warmer.
→ Tried Ember as the line colour. It fails contrast at small sizes, so the warmth comes from Crema grounds instead.

Yasmin: blends and single origins look the same on the shelf.
→ Eucalypt for single origin, Crema for blends.

Both: worried brown-on-brown disappears.
→ Bark only on light grounds, never on Eucalypt (2.4:1).

stickies.title: Today
stickies.body:
1. 250 g bag — Crema ground test
2. Kerning pass on the wordmark
3. Export sleeve proofs at 100%

stickies.title: Printer
stickies.body: Needs CMYK + spot colour refs for the bags by @+8d. Ask about uncoated stock.

desks.title: Sign-up flow redesign — usability round 2
desks.description: Six moderated sessions on the new sign-up flow for a household budgeting app: what broke, how badly, and what changes in the design file before engineering picks it up.
desks.brief:
## Sign-up flow redesign — usability round 2

**Product** Pennywell, a household budgeting app · **Flow** 5 steps, welcome to invite partner
**Round 2** 6 moderated sessions, new users, on mobile
**Engineering pick-up** @+3d · **Round 3** @+6d, 5 new participants, same script

### What round 2 was for
Round 1 lost people at bank connect. The redesign added a visible skip-for-now route and moved goals earlier. Round 2 checks whether that worked, and what it broke.

### Result
3 of 6 finished sign-up without help (round 1: 1 of 6). 10 findings, 2 of them blockers — both now designed. **Budget setup is the new pain point:** 3 findings, 9 participant hits.

### Ready for engineering when
- Bank connect and the keypad fix have every state drawn: default, loading, error, empty
- Copy is final, not placeholder
- The category list decision is made: grouped list or search-first

callout.title: Budget setup is the new pain point
callout.body: Three findings and nine participant hits — more than any other step. The keypad fix is designed; the 24-category list and the empty budget after skipping bank connect are still open, and both go into round 3.

rows.finding: Welcome didn't say the app is free
Didn't trust bank connect — what's shared?
Wanted to set a goal later
Skipped bank connect, hit an empty budget
Number keypad hid the Next button

children.label: Move to after the first weekly summary

blocks.p: A short what-we-can-see and what-we-can't panel before the connect button. 4 of 6 hesitated here; the two who didn't had used a budgeting app before.

blocks.h4: 2. Invite partner moves out of sign-up

blocks.p: 5 of 6 found it pushy before they had seen a budget. It becomes a prompt after the first weekly summary, when there is something worth sharing.
Still exploring a grouped list against search-first. Both go into round 3 as an A/B, same script.

ul: Goal presets stay, cut from eight to four — 4 of 6 picked one
Five steps stay five; the progress bar just has to say so

notes.title: Session patterns
notes.body:
- P1, P3, P4 and P6 paused 5+ seconds on the bank connect button; P2 and P5 had used a budgeting app before
- Nobody used the back arrow — they tapped the progress bar instead
- Two people asked out loud whether it costs anything
- Five of six hesitated at invite partner; P4 said they'd do it together later, at home

Round 3 keeps the same script so the numbers compare.

stickies.title: Before engineering pick-up
stickies.body:
Due @+3d:
Bank connect: all 4 states
Keypad fix: redlines
Final copy for the free-app line

stickies.title: Ask Hamid
stickies.body: Can bank connect list the providers before consent, or is that a compliance problem?
